newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end down and on support, trade brisk.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end down and on support, trade brisk.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed lower on the day after the most-active September contract failed to reach its upside target in early trade, floor sources said.
Follow-through fund buying carried the spot month to the day's high of 78.00 cents but failed to push the contract to its upside target of 78.25 cents.
The buying dried up and local profit-taking emerged to pare gains and pressure the contract below unchanged.
September eased to the day's low of 75.75 cents, just below the four-day moving average of 75.80 cents where traders pegged near-term support.
September closed on support at 75.80 cents, down 1.35 cents. The rest of the board settled 1.95 to 0.65 lower.
"The fundamentals are so overwhelmingly negative," a juice broker said. "The only hope is that the mini-freeze last winter did more damage than anyone thought."

Analysts said record crops in the U.S. and Brazil are likely to keep pressure on the market until a much-awaited private estimate of the 1997/98 U.S. crop by the private firm Citrus Consulting International is released.
"That estimate will set the tone for the next couple of months until the USDA releases its estimate in October," the broker said.
Citrus Consulting International will issue its estimate on August 14.
An estimated 5,000 lots changed hands on the day compared with Tuesday's official 5,398 lots. Market sources said short-covering accounted for the bulk of Tuesday's volume.
